title: Prevention, mitigation and preparedness

2026-11-20T13:23:39Z autoreview: cleared with the fix (a wording)

match.reason: The bank point teaches the same prevention, mitigation and preparedness idea, but it is written as a Year 7 card with examples from other states, and the Stage 5 course needs a card pitched at its depth with NSW-based examples, so a new point is the safer match.

draft.title: Prevention, mitigation and preparedness
card: Prevention
stops harm before it starts. For example, a council bans building on a floodplain.
Mitigation
reduces the effects of harm that may still happen. For example, a levee reduces how far floodwater spreads.
Preparedness
gets people ready to respond when harm happens. For example, a family practises a bushfire evacuation plan.
The three work together. Each acts at a different point: before the harm, in limiting its effects, and in readiness to respond.
draft.remember: Prevention stops it, mitigation reduces it, preparedness readies people to respond.

a.q: A town in the Hunter plants no new homes in an area prone to landslides. Which approach is this?
opts: Prevention
Mitigation
Preparedness
Response
a.why: Keeping homes out of the area stops the harm before it starts, so it is prevention. Mitigation would reduce the effects on homes already there.
a.clue: Does it stop the harm before it starts?

b.q: A school in Lismore runs a flood drill so students know where to go. Which approach is this?
opts: Preparedness, as it readies people to respond
Prevention, as it stops floods from happening
Mitigation, as it reduces how much water falls
Prevention, as it removes homes from the floodplain
b.why: A drill gets people ready to respond when a flood happens, so it is preparedness. It does not stop the flood or change how much water arrives, so it is not prevention or mitigation.
b.clue: Does the drill change the flood, or the people's readiness?

b.best: Preparedness, as it readies people to respond

problems.detail: "plants no new homes" is confusing: homes are not planted. It should read something like "allows no new homes" or "bans new homes" in an area prone to landslides.
